name: load-keys-dialog
covers: With no archive open, File > Load TACT Keys… opens the native file dialog, a key file is picked by typing its path, and the status bar reports how many keys were loaded. Needs no game install.

phases.name: open the file dialog
phases.note: KDE's file dialog belongs to xdg-desktop-portal-kde; the config lists it under helpers. On macOS the dialog is a sheet inside the main window (pattern null), so the phase waits for its Cancel button instead.

phases.name: go to folder
phases.note: The macOS Open sheet has no path field until Cmd+Shift+G opens the Go-to sheet, whose text field takes focus. A key combination is real input, so the runner raises the app first.

phases.name: pick the key file
phases.note: The filename field has no name; it is the text field holding focus when the dialog opens. On macOS it is the Go-to sheet's field: Return selects the typed file in the panel, which enables Open (the sheet itself is also named Open, so the button is learned with role button).

phases.name: keys are loaded
phases.note: A wait step, not a check: step fields expand $SMOKE and check names do not. The status bar names the file it read.

notes: Needs no game install. On Linux the config needs helpers: ["xdg-desktop-portal"]; the app may run on native Wayland or XWayland, because the only typing goes into the dialog. The final no_window check needs a bad-ass-mcp that counts a helper's open dialogs (bad-ass-mcp PR #34); older versions fail it with 'unexpected window'. Linux run 2026-11-12 (SteamOS, KDE): passed on native Wayland and on XWayland. Linux values are for KDE's dialog only; the GTK portal and Windows dialogs differ (see the table in smoke/README.md) and are not in this script yet. macOS run 2026-11-12 (macOS 26.6.2, bad-ass-mcp ed0374d): passed with the plain bam.json, no helpers. The Open sheet lives in the main window, so the dialog phases run there (window null); the path goes through Cmd+Shift+G's Go-to sheet and Return, which selects the file and enables Open. Keys are sent without a window id: on macOS a key posted to the app's process never reaches an Open panel. The final no_window check is Linux-only; on macOS the run checks the sheet's Cancel button is gone.
